title_zh: 情景喜剧：客厅里的笑声
title_en: Chinese TV Dramas (13/20): Sitcoms, Laughter in the Living Room
note_en: The 把 construction moves the object in front of the verb when the point is what happens to it: 爸爸……把整个客厅弄得一团糟 "Dad turns the whole living room into a total mess." English simply says "verb + object," but Chinese uses 把 + object + verb + result (here 弄得一团糟, "messed up into a heap") to stress how the object ends up.

sentences.en: Anna thought that maybe it was precisely because each sitcom episode tells a complete, self-contained story, along with the genre's typical gag, a misunderstanding that sets off a chain of ever more absurd events whose truth always comes out by the end of the episode, that you can pick up a sitcom anytime, even if you haven't been following along. Even a celebrity's occasional cameo in a bonus episode doesn't break that easy mood; for that one evening, it simply becomes part of the long-familiar comedy of errors playing out in the living room.
